'''Danocia''', officially the '''Republic of Danocia''', is a country located in [[Northern Ayuma]]. It is bordered by [[Estijan]] to the south and [[Koruch]] to the north, and the [[Yshatan Gulf]] to the west. Danocia spans an area of [[List of countries and dependencies by area|749,885 square kilometres (289,532 sq mi)]] with a population of [[List of countries and dependencies by population|2.0 million]]. The country has a tundra climate and is administratively divided into eight regions. [[Tazmirak]] is the capital and largest city; it is administered separately as a city with special status.

For most of the medieval period, the lands of modern-day Danocia were ruled by independent [[coastal settlements]]. Around 1320, these lands came fully under the Grand Duchy of Danocia and subsequently by the [[Danocian Kingdom]];

This period lasted for 100 years until [[Estijan Huan]] made Danocia a tributary in 1519 AFA, placing Danocia within the Estijan sphere for the first time, with the country later becoming a colony in 1645. In the aftermath of the [[Nationalist coup]] in 1678 AFA, different states arose competing for legitimacy amid the crisis. During the [[Red War]], Danocian men were drafted at a much higher rate than those of Estijan, [[devastating Danocias popuation]], which lost about a quarter of its population and half of its economic resources. The republic was home to a widespread and diverse [[pro-state insurgent movement]], which dominated politics until well into the 1730s, overseeing Danocia's transformation from an agrarian to an [[wikipedia:Industrial_organization|industrial economy]]. Becoming a [[protectorate]] in 1730.

The parliament of the republic proclaimed the sovereignty of Danocia in May 1740 AFA, and during the dissolution of the [[Collapse of the Huan]], Danocia gained independence on August 1740. Following the adoption of a [[new constitution]] in 1744, [[Xiala Walenco]] was elected Danocia's first president in the country's first and only free election after independence, and has served as president ever since. [[Xiala Walenco|Walenco]] heads a highly centralised [[wikipedia:Authoritarianism|authoritarian government]]. Danocia ranks low in international measurements of freedom of the press and civil liberties. After a short Estijan invasion after an atempted coup againt [[Xiala Walenco|Walenco]] in 1747, Danocia has continued [[several Huan-era policies]], such as [[wikipedia:State_ownership|state ownership]] of large sections of the economy. In 1750, Danocia and Estijan signed a treaty for greater cooperation.

Modern Danocia is a unitary, democratic nation-state. It is a developing country and ranks [[List of countries by Krali Total Development Index|97th on the Krali Total Development Index]] as of 1763. Its economy is primarily based on industrial output and mineral extraction.
